newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- CENTRICA REVEALS LIST OF DISPUTES

The trading and service business being demerged by British Gas, Centrica, is involved in a series of legal disputes over payments for gas supplies in addition to its take-or-pay contracts. A demerger document shows that a dispute, involving 51 million stg in payment for gas from fields in the North Sea, is now in the hands of an independent expert. The company is also seeking compensation in a dispute over gas delivered through the Brent pipeline system to the Shell -Esso terminal in Grampian.
-- LADBROKE TO GIVE DETAILS OF HILTON LINK

Hotel and betting group Ladbroke is to unveil further details of its worldwide alliance with America's Hilton Hotels Corp. Last summer, the two companies signed a deal to reunite the Hilton hotel brand. Hilton Hotels controls the Hilton name in America and Ladbroke owns the brand in the rest of the world. Hilton Hotels will take an initial five percent stake in Ladbroke, increasing up to a maximum of 20 percent.
-- FUND MANAGERS EYE PROPERTY STOCKS

A Gallup poll for stockbrokers Merrill Lynch shows that fund managers are switching their portfolio preferences to smaller companies' shares and property. This suggests that they believe that the economy will continue to grow at above the average rate. Fund managers who are net buyers of property outnumber net sellers by 20 percent, while two months ago the margin was one percent.
THE TIMES
-- INSTITUTE OF DIRECTORS TO CALL FOR INTEREST RATE INCREASE

The Institute of Directors is to urge the government and the Bank of England to agree a rise in interest rates as their latest evidence from business shows strong economic growth and an increase in inflationary pressures. The call for higher interest rates is aimed at stopping any resurgence in inflation. It is also expected that the monthly monetary meeting between Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England governor Eddie George will lead to a further increase in rates.
-- COACH GROUP IN WELCOME BREAK BID

Privatised coach operator National Express is one of the six shortlisted bidders for motorway services business Welcome Break, which is being sold by Granada for 380 million stg. This points to a radical diversification for National Express, which was sold to its management as a long distance coach operator but has since moved into rail and airports. Others shortlisted include Cinven and Whitbread.
-- FORD JOBS THREAT AT HALEWOOD

Mounting speculation that Ford's Halewood car plant on Merseyside is to close has led to an attempt by union leaders to save 4,500 jobs. Ford is believed to be considering moving the production of the new Escort model from the plant to continental Europe. Ford managers are to demand tough concessions from unions to increase efficiency, which could include 500 job losses and a two-year no-strike agreement.
THE GUARDIAN
-- AUSTRIA BANK MERGER AGREED

The Social Democrats and the conservative People's Party, Austria's leading political parties, have agreed to end 50 years' partisan control of competing banks by agreeing a merger of the country's two main banking groups. The government will sell its 70 percent stake in Creditanstalt to Bank Austria for 17.16 billion schillings. Bank Austria will spearhead privatisation of the country's top-heavy banking system.
-- CASH OFFERED TO YOUNG INVESTORS

UBS subsidiary Centrade Private Bank Switzerland is to offer compensation to 90 investors who claim to have lost $26.7 million in foreign exchange deals carried out in Jersey by independent dealer Robert Young. CI is offering to repay their trading losses together with the appropriate interest, and compensation could amount to between $13 million and $15 million. The trades were effected though CI and the bank strongly denies any legal liability.
-- WH SMITH FAILS TO FILL VITAL GAP IN REVIVAL PLAN

News agency and record chain WH Smith has failed to find a replacement for Simon Burke, one of its key executives, despite pressure from investors for improved performance. The company will announce better interim profits this month and admits it has been unable to recruit a managing director for Virgin Our Price, one of the group's fastest-growing and most well known brand names.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- CABLE AND WIRELESS 5.0 BLN STG DEAL RUNS INTO SNAGS

The April deadline for the five billion stg merger of Cable and Wireless's Mercury phone subsidiary with three cable companies is unlikely to be achieved after a series of problems. There is growing disagreement between the companies involved. Insiders blame a clash of cultures between C&W and the smaller cable operators. A large team of management consultants from the Boston Consulting Group and public relations advisers Brunswick have been called in to rectify the problem.
-- MAGNOX MERGER DEADLINE AGREED

Hopes have risen for a pre-election merger between the state-owned company which runs ageing nuclear power stations, Magnox Electric, and the reprocessing organisation, British Nuclear Fuels. The two sides have agreed to a provisional deadline in negotiations with the government. Ministers aim to transfer responsibility for Magnox Electric to BNFL and talks became deadlocked because of BNFL's unhappiness at having to take over part of Magnox's 8.9 billion stg decommissioning costs.
-- SEARS SHOES TOLD TO PULL ITS SOCKS UP

Retailing giant Sears is ready to sell or demerge its shoe business if there is no improvement by the summer. Chief executive Liam Strong is under increasing pressure from large shareholders to resign or institute a breakup of the group after a profits warning last week. He is hoping that spring ranges can still revive the fortunes of the British Shoe Corp operation.
